Order 
This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants assailing the award dated 26.07.2008 passed by the Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena (M.P.) in Claim Case No.13/2008, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation, seeking enhancement thereof.
2.

entities.text: Fourth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that on 28.11.2007 at about 4:00 PM, Malua was standing on the side of Baidagaon Road along with her husband Rajveer, Parimal, and Bharat Singh.

At that time,
respondent No.2, while driving a motorcycle bearing registration No. MP 06 HB 6770, owned by respondent No.1, in a rash and negligent manner and at high speed, struck Malua, resulting in a serious accident.

As a consequence of the said accident, Malua sustained grievous injuries and,
despite medical treatment, she succumbed to the injuries on 07.12.2007.

The incident was reported to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:228 2 MA-1329-2008 police, an FIR was registered, and after due investigation, the charge-sheet was filed.
3. On account of the death of Malua, the appellants/claimants filed a claim petition seeking compensation before the Claims Tribunal.
The respondents appeared and filed their written statements denying the averments made in the claim petition.

4. Upon appreciation of the pleadings and evidence adduced by both parties, the Claims Tribunal allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.1,86,000/-.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contended that the Claims Tribunal committed a grave error in assessing the income of the deceased at a very low figure of Rs.15,000/- per annum.
It was argued that in the absence of documentary evidence regarding income, the Tribunal was duty-bound to assess the income in accordance with the Minimum Wages Act.
It was further contended that the Tribunal failed to grant future prospects and compensation under conventional heads such as loss of consortium, loss of estate, and funeral expenses.

On these grounds,
enhancement of compensation was prayed for.

6. Learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company filed cross- objections under Order 41 Rule 22 of CPC and contended that as per Ex.P-3, it was mentioned that the deceased was sitting on a motorcycle being driven by her brother and that due to the motorcycle turning turtle, she sustained injuries and died during treatment.

It was submitted that this fact was not considered by the Claims Tribunal, and therefore, there was no rash or NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:228 3 MA-1329-2008 negligent driving by the insured vehicle.
On this basis, it was argued that the Insurance Company was not liable to pay compensation.

Reliance was placed upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Insurance Company Limited v. Premlata Shukla and Others, reported in (2007) 13 SCC 476, to contend that a party cannot rely upon a part of a document favourable to it while ignoring the remaining part.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record of the Claims Tribunal.

First consideration of Cross-Objections:-
8. Insurance Company relied upon the Ex.P-3 in which, it was mentioned that "   
          ---
                      
                   "
9. Upon perusal of the entire document, it is evident that Ex.P-3 was prepared by the Investigating Officer.
However, Ex.P-3 does not disclose that its contents were recorded by the Investigating Officer on the basis of information supplied by the family members of the deceased.

It was incumbent upon the Insurance Company to establish this fact by examining the Investigating Officer, who was the best person to explain the source of information and the manner in which the contents of Ex.P-3 were recorded.
The Insurance Company, however, failed to adduce the evidence of the Investigating Officer, and consequently, the said fact has not been duly proved.
In the absence of such proof, no benefit can be extended to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:228 4 MA-1329-2008 Insurance Company on the basis of Ex.P-3.

entities.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:228 4 MA-1329-2008 Insurance Company
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Insurance Company has thus failed to lead any cogent evidence in this regard.
Accordingly, the cross- objection filed by the Insurance Company is devoid of substance and is hereby rejected.

2 Now, consideration on enhancement of compensation:-
10.

So far the contention raised by counsel for the appellants for enhancement of compensation is concerned, Claims Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased as Rs. 15,000/- per year which is on the lower side.

So, in view of the judgments in Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v.
Bansal Roadways , 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134 , when documentary proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the Minimum Wages Act.

sentences.text: 11. In the present case, the accident occurred on 28.11.2007.
At the relevant time, as per the Minimum Wages Act, the monthly income of an unskilled labourer was Rs. 2,651/- per month.
Therefore, the income of the deceased is required to be assessed at Rs.2,651/- per month.

12. With regard to loss of income, including future prospects, in light of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled to an addition of 40% towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. , reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121,
even if the age of the deceased is taken into consideration, the appropriate multiplier to be applied is "18" instead of "17".
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:228 5 MA-1329-2008 13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, appellants-claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AMOUN  Income Rs.2,651 X 12=31

After adding Future Prospects@40% Rs.44,537/-
 after adding dependency 3/4 Rs.33,403/-
 Loss of Income Rs.601254/-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000X6 = Rs

Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
 Total Compensation = 
14.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.8,71,254/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.1,86,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.6,85,254/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
15. Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, and the compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.6,85,254/-.

The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal, from the date of filing of the claim petition till its final Rajveer vs Shrikrishan Prajapati on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151483555/
3 realization.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellants within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

16. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:228 6 MA-1329-2008 Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
17. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
